WIRING ONLY, covers 0 BY DESIGN. Every JS line this file's stages touch is already claimed by the builder that owns it (RoadBuilder.cs for citymap.js:871/873 + src/roads.js, BridgeBuilder.cs for :874-875 + src/bridges.js, TunnelBuilder/TunnelCuts.cs for :726/:876, RiverSheet.cs for :583-724/:880, WaterBodies.cs for :878, GrassCover.cs for :8266-8420, InfraBuilder.cs for src/infra.js, CutTerrainBuilder.cs for :3961-4057). Re-claiming them here would be the derived-by-subtraction over-claim the skill warns about. What this file adds is a CALLER, which the coverage number cannot express.

THE GAP IT CLOSES. `grep -c` in BOTH scene builders (Editor/BuildPlayableScene.cs, Editor/BuildCityRender.cs) was 0 for RoadBuilder, RiverSheet, BridgeBuilder, TunnelBuilder, InfraBuilder, WaterBodies, GrassCover, CutTerrainBuilder and RoadSignsStreetlights. Their only driver was CityLoader's RunCritical/RunScenery stages, and CityLoader has NO runtime caller anywhere -- only Editor/Probes/CityLoadProbe.cs. So the roads with real OSM widths/lanes/layers, the Mtkvari sheet, the quays, the bridges, the tunnel bores and the grass sheet were all probe-verified and drawn nowhere. This file runs CityLoader.RunCritical's DATA half, in its own stage order, once per domain, and three new renderers read it.

WHY A SHARED CACHE AND NOT THREE PRIVATE CityData.Load()s (the precedent every other scenery renderer follows): TerrainSampler.GroundCut is how a planned tunnel trench reaches every later height read, and it is hooked onto ONE sampler. Three samplers = at most one of them cut = the road deck, the river sheet, the grass sheet and the cut-terrain patch each draped on a DIFFERENT surface, which is the 'roads under grass' defect class re-created structurally.

PAIRED WITH A ONE-LINE CHANGE IN Editor/BuildPlayableScene.cs: that file calls TerrainBuilder.Build(city.Terrain) with no exclusion, so the 2,746 cells a river bank or a tunnel trench passes through are drawn BOTH coarse and refined. Passing CityGroundData.RefinedCells() as the second argument is the fix; the cut-terrain patch here carries its own MeshCollider and CombatTerrainTag so the excluded cells are never a hole in the ground.

ASSET BUG FOUND AND FIXED HERE (data, not code): unity/Assets/Art/Props/infra_kit.fbx and embankment_kit.fbx each contained exactly ONE mesh ('arch_rib' / 'bal_pier') with a single 'PaletteMaterial001'. They were converted from public/models/*.glb, which are themselves palette-joined -- an early run of tools/compress_models.sh, before that script grew its `--join false --palette false --prune-attributes false` guard and the comment explaining it. Every kit[name] lookup therefore failed, in Unity AND in the shipped JS build (src/infra.js:115 `const k = kit[name]; if (!k ...) return 0;`), so the quays, balustrades, kerbs, crossings, bus stops, portals and lamp columns rendered nowhere in either. The intact kits survive in models_raw/ (23 + 5 named nodes, real inf_*/emb_* material names) and were re-converted with tools/glb_batch_fbx.py; the .meta files and their GUIDs are untouched.

note: BUG FIX, no new coverage. This renderer submitted ZERO draws per frame from everywhere -- TotalInstances=596 across 10 batches, LastTickDrawCalls=0 at Old Town and in both sheds. The cause was not the distance but what it was measured FROM: PlaceShared/PlaceVariantStatues built ONE batch per variant whose Bounds spanned the whole city, and handed Bounds.center.x to CityCulling as the chunk centre, so the 207 street statues and 91 busts were culled against the distance from the camera to the CENTROID OF ALL OF THEM across a ~20 km city. src/landmarks.js:1459-1474 never had the problem because placeInstanced calls citymap._placeChunkedInstanced(geo, mat, items, makeMatrix, 1500, false, 2200) -- 1500 m cells, each with its own centre, drawn to 2,200 m. All three numbers now come from that call site (the constant was also 2500, not 2200), and both statue layers and their plinth/pillar go through ChunkedInstancer.Place.
